name: Consolidated Edison (CECONY)
territory: New York City and Westchester County
_dc_note: NYC data centre load estimated ~1,500 MW (2026). dc_load_growth_rate calibrated to 6%/yr (down from an initially-proposed 12%/yr, which compounds to a 5.0% total-peak CAGR over 24 years — roughly double Con Edison's published load growth forecast). At 6%/yr, combined with BASELINE_LOAD_GROWTH (0.5%) and ELECTRIFICATION_RAMP, total peak CAGR is 2.4% and BAU 2050 monthly bill is ~$426 — both consistent with Con Edison's published load growth forecast and with pre-segmentation model results (~$424). NYISO large load project requests show a significant data centre pipeline for NYC/Westchester supporting continued growth at this segment-specific rate. Source: Con Edison 2025 DSIP; NYISO 2025 reliability needs assessment.
_sources: Rate base & capital: Joint Proposal, NYPSC Case 25-E-0072, approved January 22 2026 (annual_capex_m = average of RY1 $4,550M / RY2 $4,474M / RY3 $4,712M; total_revenue_m estimated). ROE and equity_ratio: Joint Proposal 2026-2028. Customers, peak_demand_mw, annual_energy_gwh: Con Edison 2024 Form 10-K. DER baseline: CLCPA progress reports; NYSERDA data.
_notes: capacity_market / capacity_market_zone are descriptive metadata pointing to shared/capacity_markets/NYISO.json; not yet consumed by the model engine at this refactoring stage — CAPACITY_COST_START remains a notebook-level global.
_class_shares_note: EIA Form 861, 2024 (Sales_Ult_Cust_2024.xlsx), Consolidated Edison Co-NY Inc, NY: bundled (Part A) + delivery-only (Part C) rows, so retail-choice load is included. Residential sales 13,643,968 of 52,425,970 MWh = 26.0%; residential customers 3,064,038 of 3,646,787 = 84.0%. Used only when CAPACITY_SAVINGS_ALLOCATION = 'sales_share' (CORRECTED): the residential capacity credit is scaled by sales share / customer share.

forward_assumptions._note: Forward assumptions for the layer engine (engine/layers.py). Data only for v1.0 / CORRECTED, which do not read this section. Levels: for layer assumptions, 'low' is the value that gives customers a SMALLER shared-savings effect and 'high' a LARGER one, so all-low / all-high bracket the outcome. For load-growth and price-growth assumptions (system_needs, projection, capacity price growth) 'low'/'high' mean lower/higher growth. 'derived' = computed from a cited input by the stated method; '_VERIFY' = judgement or placeholder needing a utility-specific source.

transmission_growth.source: Assumption: central = INFLATION_RATE; high reflects transmission build-out

program_surcharge_growth.source: Assumption: BAU surcharge rates grow with inflation (policy-driven)

cost_per_mw_yr.source: Placeholder for a blended EE / electrification / DR portfolio. Anchors: Brattle Ontario (2026) $50/kW-yr DER capacity cost (high case, DR-like resources; cited in notebook Section 1 OPEX_RATIO note); Pepco Rider R-DLC pays $40-80 per controlled device per year (Pepco MD tariff p. 49). Efficiency and electrification deliver peak kW at higher cost, so central $150/kW-yr and low $300/kW-yr are judgement.
